observations: Photo 0 shows a black electronic keyboard with 61 keys, placed on top of a Roland keyboard.
The keyboard has a central LCD screen, multiple buttons, knobs, and two speakers on either side.
The keys appear to be standard white and black, with some visible wear and dust.
The keyboard is not powered on; the screen is off.
The keyboard is resting on a surface with plastic wrapping, suggesting it may be new or recently unpacked.
No visible damage to the casing or keys, but the screen is not lit.

claims.evidence: No photo shows this clearly enough to read.

risks.risk: The keyboard may not be functional (e.g., screen not working, keys not responding).
risks.proof: A video or photo showing the keyboard powered on, with the screen lit and keys being pressed to demonstrate functionality.

risks.risk: The keyboard may have internal damage or wear not visible in the photo.
risks.proof: A close-up video of the keys being pressed, sound output, and any visible signs of wear or damage.
risks.if_unproven: priced as used with potential hidden defects

risks.risk: The keyboard may be a counterfeit or non-genuine unit.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the serial number and model label, ideally with a close-up of the Yamaha logo and model text.

proof_requests: Video or photo of the keyboard powered on, showing the screen lit and keys responding.
Close-up photo of the model label and serial number.
Photo of the underside or back of the keyboard to check for damage or wear.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
